sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate is the largest species in Australia, clearly distinct from the other Australian species of the genus. The soldier is closest to M. broomensis (original combination), from which it differs in: head relatively shorter and wider; mandibles shorter and of similar thickness; frontal tubercles slightly narrower at the base, distinctly sharper and more horizontal at the apex; antennae 14-segmented, segments 2, 3 and 4 about equal in length, the remaining segments distinctly shorter and narrower; anterior corners of the labrum usually less developed, but sometimes shaped as in M. broomensis.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Largest species in Australia. Head ochraceous brown, the postclypeus and pronotum paler, the labrum, antennae and maxillary palps yellow, the meso- and metanotum mainly warm yellowish brown, the sternites orange-yellow with the sides tinged pale brown, the legs and pleurites very pale, the pleurites tinged dark brown in addition. Head, thorax and abdomen densely hairy. Head very wide, distinctly rounded posteriorly and narrowing anteriorly, the vertex flat. Compound eyes large and projecting. Ocelli rather small, variable in size, far from the compound eyes, the inner margin raised. Fontanelle small, oval, with a secondary prolongation. Postclypeus more than half as long as wide (0.36—0.40 mm × 0.62—0.66 mm), the anterior margin slightly concave. Frons with a distinct triangular area; frontal mark distinct; between the anterior margin of the secondary fontanelle and the anterior margin of the frontal mark two pale oblique lines. Apical tooth of the mandibles distinctly larger than tooth 2. Antennae 15-segmented, the segmentation variable; segment 3 usually shortest, segment 2 sometimes shorter than segment 3, segments 3 and 4 about equal; segment 5 slightly larger than segment 2; segments 5—14 progressively longer; segment 15 long oval, widest in the middle. Pronotum very long and wide, wider than the head, the anterior margin shallowly concave without a median cleft, the posterior margin truncate in the middle, with a broad V-shaped mark in the middle, on each side near the anterior margin a transverse linear mark, and another linear mark along the midline from the posterior margin to the base of the V-shaped mark. Posterior margin of the mesonotum wider than that of the metanotum and more widely notched. Wings without a radial vein; radial sector very dark and stout; media slightly above the middle of the wing, usually with 2—3 branches; cubitus slightly below the middle of the wing, with about 10 branches. Measurements: length with wings 13.50—14.50 mm, length without wings 6.80—7.50 mm, head length (to apex of labrum) 1.39—1.50 mm, head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 0.77—0.84 mm, head width 1.43 mm, greatest diameter of compound eye 0.40 mm, ocellus length 0.12 mm, pronotum length 0.95 mm, width 1.54—1.57 mm, forewing length 10.00 mm, width 3.00 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The differences from M. broomensis are given under Diagnostic characters. Measurements: total length 4.50—5.00 mm (from the mandibles crossed at the base to the apex of the left mandible), head length (to apex of frontal tubercle) 1.68—1.98 mm, head width 1.17—1.39 mm, pronotum length 0.33—0.35 mm, width 0.66—0.73 mm.

note: Adapted from the species-level description in Hill (1942), originally in English; the alate is described by Hill for the first time (hitherto undescribed), the soldier is a comparative account based on the 1927 original description, and the worker is listed only as a morphotype without description. OCR problems: the heading "Mirotermes ( Mirotermes) quadratus Hill" lacks a space; "Rolotype" is Holotype; "Pig. 310/311" is Fig.; "f from" is , from; "(l 4 segments)" is (14 segments); "1,17 - 1.39*", "1.*54", "d ase" and "m a nest of nervoaus" are broken or misread words; "5 '-shaped" is an error for V-shaped. The type locality Northern Territory: Stapleton agrees with the list. Distribution (Stapleton, Marrakai, Brock's Creek) and biology (the original description based on one soldier collected in a nest of nervosus; the other series collected 30/9 to 20/10, sympatric with A. darwini and sharing underground galleries) are not translated into the morphology section.
